next_step: POC streaming latency test with staged traffic; finalize pricing for reserved capacity if SLOs met
blockers: first-token latency <1.5s (p95) not yet proven on hosted
notes: Company snapshot: Mid-market SaaS that provides in-app customer support for B2B SaaS customers; strong PLG motion; product-led growth + sales for larger accounts.
Primary interest: replace slow rule-based routing + multiple knowledge connectors with a single streaming chat agent. Focus on conversational handoff, tool-calling to ticketing system.
Latency SLO: explicit — <1.5s first-token p95 for agent responses; streaming required for perceived responsiveness.
Model preference: wants tested with open/quantized variants (they mentioned Llama-2 style family) but open to Redwood-curated models if latency/cost tradeoff is good.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit cost < $0.003/token effective in peak scenarios.
Security: SAML SSO mandatory for admin console; SOC2 mandatory; audit logs + KMS for encryption; US-only residency for customer data.
Ops/observability asks: per-route token + latency breakdown, traceable websocket session IDs, canary rollout support, automatic fallback to smaller model on overload.
Quote from VP Product (2/18 demo): "We need the chat to feel instant — if the agent stalls our NPS drops. If you can hit 1.5s first token at scale, we can talk committed capacity."
They run ~250 concurrent live chat sessions during normal business hours; ramp to 600 concurrent during major releases — POC should include both steady-state and burst tests.
Decision path: Product VP (technical), Head of Infra (SRE), Legal (data residency), Procurement. Procurement involved once POC passes latency + security checks.
Customer readiness: engineering team available for POC integrations (websocket streaming + function/tool calling hooks).
